THE "ATTACK C" FALSE-FRAMING CHECK, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE WHOLE CHANGE. The historical defect was `facts_incomplete` being reported with the same words as a genuine count ("N record(s) found ... none matching"), i.e. "could not check" wearing the costume of "checked, found nothing". I asserted on the actual string: the fail-closed reason contains "could not verify" -> True, and contains "record(s) found" -> **False**. The two outcomes are now genuinely distinct sentences, not variants. This is the repo's own named DEFECT PATTERN (HANDOFF item 5) being closed properly rather than renamed.

=== THE BIG CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS DOCUMENTED HONESTLY ===
Because the Codex adapter collects no repo facts, `event.repo is None` on EVERY Codex event -- so arming `deny` after this change denies every genuine publish on Codex, unconditionally. That is a large, easily-missed consequence and the first thing I went looking for. docs/rules/lwb-proof-required.md's "Known gap: Codex" section states it outright, calls it "the correct consequence of 1.2's own framing, not a bug", and draws the right operational conclusion: do not arm `deny` in any policy a Codex session might run under until the Codex adapter populates RepoFacts. core/policy/default.json still ships `warn`, so nothing changes for today's installs. I could not have asked for better disclosure, and I checked the claim rather than accepting it: no RepoFacts/repo_facts reference exists anywhere under adapters/codex/.

I reviewed #53 earlier in this same run.
